Subject: Locality & legal-hold carveouts — DPA redlines question

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA yesterday. Our legal team reviewed and inserted a couple of redlines around the retention and deletion sections that touch on legal holds and snapshot/backups. Two quick areas we need clarity on before we proceed:

1) If we implement a court-ordered legal hold on a subset of Acme users, will Redwood retain on-disk snapshots or backups that would otherwise be subject to deletion while the hold is active? If so, where are those backups stored (regionally) and how long are they kept?

2) Our procurement team needs an operational certificate of deletion (proof-of-deletion) for any retained backups once the hold is released. Is Redwood able to provide a signed certificate with scope and timestamp?

I attached our annotated DPA (DPA-redline-Acme-20270501.docx) with line comments. Can you confirm Redwood's posture and proposed alternative language we can accept? Also flagged a paragraph re: \"onshore-only backups\" — we may need a narrow carveout for our EU-sited data for regulatory needs.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we have a legal review call next Wednesday.

Best,
Emma
Emma Lawson
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Corporation
Attachment: DPA-redline-Acme-20270501.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Locality & legal-hold carveouts — DPA redlines question

Emma — thanks for the redlines and for the clear asks. Quick clarifying Qs before we propose language back:

- When you say \"subset of Acme users\" for legal hold, do you mean tenant-wide (all users under a single account) or a user/email-level selection? Implementation differs.
- Are you asking for a persistent, immutable copy of snapshots to be retained in a specific country, or are you asking only that onshore copies (for regulatory reasons) are exempted from normal automated deletion?

High-level options we can offer now (we'll have legal craft the exact DPA wording):

Option A — Jurisdictional carveout: Redwood will retain onshore backup snapshots for EU-sited data if Acme specifically requests a jurisdictional carveout at activation time. These snapshots are stored in the EU region and marked with a legal_hold tag; standard snapshot TTLs remain unless a hold is applied.

Option B — Legal-hold tag + export: When a legal hold is applied to selected accounts, Redwood marks retained artifacts (snapshots/backup copies) with a legal_hold flag and suspends automated deletion for the duration of the hold. Once the hold is released, Redwood will run a certified deletion workflow within X business days and provide an evidence package.

Option C — Short-term hold with certified retention: For regulatory needs, we can offer a limited certified retention (e.g., 90 days) for onshore backups with a signed deletion certificate upon expiry or earlier release.

Laura — can you weigh in on the certified deletion timelines that are realistic operationally? Soojin — can you confirm whether our onshore backup architecture supports marking per-tenant snapshots for hold and producing deletion certificates?

We can propose concrete redline text by EOD Monday. If that timeline doesn't work for your legal review call, tell us and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Locality & legal-hold carveouts — proposed DPA language

Emma / Jordan — putting in legal's proposed language and operational notes below. I've also attached an editable redline that integrates the three options Jordan outlined. Key points we want to capture in the DPA:

1) Scope of Hold: A legal hold may target specific user identifiers or entire account(s) depending on Acme's written instruction. The Provider (Redwood) will apply the hold only to data categories and account identifiers explicitly listed in a written legal hold notice.

2) Storage Location: For data stored in the EU region, onshore snapshots will remain in the EU and will not be transferred outside the EU as part of the hold process unless Acme provides written consent.

3) Retention & Deletion Procedure: While a legal hold is in effect, Redwood will suspend automated deletion for artifacts tagged with legal_hold. Upon written release of the hold, Redwood will: (a) schedule deletion of retained artifacts; (b) execute deletion across primary and backup copies within a defined window; and (c) provide an executed \"Certificate of Deletion\" signed by Redwood's authorized representative.

Operational feasibility notes (for Acme's review):
- Per-tenant snapshot tagging is supported.
- Certified deletion for all backup tiers can be executed but may require a 30–60 business day window to coordinate across cold storage / archive tiers and third-party backup vendors.
- Audit logs will include a deletion job id and timestamp; we can include a scope section in the certificate enumerating objects removed.

Suggested redline for the DPA (high level):
\"Provider shall, upon receipt of a documented legal hold notice, preserve data identified in the notice by suspending automated deletion and marking retained artifacts with a legal_hold flag. Retained artifacts for EU-sited data will remain in the EU. Within 60 business days of receipt of a written release of the legal hold, Provider will complete deletion of such retained artifacts across primary and backup storage and deliver a Certificate of Deletion to Customer.\"

We're open to tightening the 60 business day window to a shorter timeline for primary storage if Acme needs it — the complexity arises for cold-archive tiers and third-party restores. Happy to discuss tradeoffs.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA-redline-Acme-20270501.docx
From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 07:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Locality & legal-hold carveouts — proposed DPA language

Laura — thanks, that language is clear and mostly acceptable. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- The 60 business day window for all tiers is longer than our internal SLA expectation. Can we separate primary/nearline (15 business days) from deep archive (60 business days)? That would be workable.
- Certification: we'll need a signed Certificate of Deletion that includes: (i) object identifiers removed; (ii) storage tier; (iii) deletion timestamps; and (iv) confirmation of region (EU). The template you attached looks close — we may add a small clause requiring Redwood to retain audit evidence for 2 years.

Also — on the onshore-only backup carveout phrase we inserted: we only need the ability to keep a jurisdiction-specific copy for the duration of the hold. If Redwood can guarantee the copy never leaves the EU and provide the certificate upon release, that will satisfy our compliance group.

Let's plan to finalize redline language by your proposed EOD Monday. We can sign off on DocuSign after that.

Thanks,
Emma
